questions.prompt: main.o needs A, A needs B, both are static archives. Which hand-written link line works with GNU ld?
options: g++ main.o -lA -lB
Both always work
Neither can work
g++ main.o -lB -lA
questions.explanation: Archives are scanned left to right; B must come after the library that needs it.

questions.prompt: A new source file is added to src/ but the project uses file(GLOB SRC src/*.cpp). The build still fails with undefined reference. What is the most likely reason?
options: The glob is evaluated at configure time; CMake has not been re-run
Static libraries ignore any new files placed in src/
ctest must be run first to register the new file
The linker cannot read source files added after the first build
questions.explanation: Re-run cmake, list sources explicitly, or use CONFIGURE_DEPENDS.

questions.prompt: A header-only math library has no .cpp files. Which CMake form describes it?
options: add_library(mathlib INTERFACE) with target_include_directories(mathlib INTERFACE include)
add_library(mathlib STATIC) with an empty source list and the headers copied in
include_directories(include) only, with no library target defined for users
add_executable(mathlib) with all of the header files listed as its sources
questions.explanation: INTERFACE targets carry usage requirements for their users but build nothing themselves.

questions.prompt: Why configure with cmake -S . -B build rather than running cmake in the source directory?
options: It disables the sanitizer flags that were previously set in the CMake cache
It makes the compiler produce faster code than an in-source build would give
It is required, because ctest only works when started from a separate directory
Generated files stay out of the source tree and several configurations can coexist
questions.explanation: Separate build directories keep the tree clean and let you keep Debug, Release and ASAN builds side by side.

questions.prompt: 12 of 80 objects include header common.hpp; each compile takes 2 s and the final link takes 5 s. How many seconds does a rebuild after touching common.hpp take? Give an integer.
questions.explanation: 12 x 2 = 24 s of compiling plus 5 s linking = 29 s.

questions.prompt: Graph: x.o needs x.cpp and common.hpp; y.o needs y.cpp and common.hpp; libxy needs x.o and y.o; tool needs libxy and tool.o; tool.o needs tool.cpp. common.hpp is edited. How many nodes (including common.hpp itself) are in the rebuild set? Integer.
questions.explanation: common.hpp, x.o, y.o, libxy, tool = 5. tool.o does not depend on common.hpp.

questions.prompt: 7 tests are registered and 1 fails. What percentage passes? Give a number with 1 decimal.

app links libA PRIVATE. libA links libB PUBLIC. libB links libC PRIVATE. libA, libB, libC each export a PUBLIC include directory. How many of these three include directories does app see when compiling? Integer.
questions.explanation: app sees libA's directory and, because libA links libB PUBLIC, libB's. libC's is private to libB.

questions.prompt: demo fails with 'fatal error: robotmath/vec2.hpp: No such file or directory' although the library compiles. Give the likely cause in CMake terms and the one-line fix.
rubric: demo is not linked with the library target, or the library does not export its include directory as PUBLIC.
Fix: target_link_libraries(demo PRIVATE robotmath) and target_include_directories(robotmath PUBLIC include).
Names the stage: preprocessing, not linking.

questions.prompt: Your team debates one big target versus many small library targets for a 200-file robot stack. Give two arguments for the split and one cost.
rubric: Precise rebuilds: a change recompiles only dependents.
Layering is enforced through the dependency graph and prevents cycles; PRIVATE hides internals.
Cost: more CMake to maintain, slower configuration and a graph to understand.

questions.prompt: libP.a has p1.o (defines fp1, needs fq1) and p2.o (defines fp2, needs fq2). libQ.a has q1.o (defines fq1, needs fp2) and q2.o (defines fq2). main.o needs fp1. Which is the shortest of these link lines that succeeds with a GNU linker?
options: main.o -lP -lQ
main.o -lQ -lP
main.o -lP -lQ -lP
main.o -lP -lQ -lP -lQ
questions.explanation: Each archive is scanned once per occurrence, in order. -lP -lQ: p1.o then q1.o are extracted, fp2 stays undefined. -lQ -lP: nothing pending when libQ is scanned, and fq1 stays undefined after p1.o. -lP -lQ -lP: the second libP scan extracts p2.o which needs fq2, but libQ is not scanned again. Only -lP -lQ -lP -lQ extracts q2.o and leaves nothing undefined.

questions.prompt: A generated header is included by 25 of 40 sources. Each compile takes 3 s and Ninja runs 8 jobs in parallel. The generator rewrites the header with different contents. Ignoring link time and assuming whole rounds of 8 jobs, how many seconds of wall-clock compile time does the rebuild take? Give an integer.
questions.explanation: All 25 dependent sources are stale, so 25 compiles run. With 8 parallel jobs that is ceil(25/8) = 4 rounds of 3 s = 12 s. (With restat = 1 and an unchanged header the answer would be 0 compiles.)

questions.prompt: Static library A links B PRIVATE, and B exports its include directory PUBLIC. Executable m links A and now needs a header of B. Explain (1) why libB.a is already on m's link line but B's include directory is not on m's compile line, and (2) the correct minimal change and the design mistake to avoid.
rubric: For a static A, CMake records the private dependency in A's interface as $<LINK_ONLY:B>: B is linked (A's objects reference it) but none of B's compile-time usage requirements propagate.
Correct change: target_link_libraries(m PRIVATE B) so that m declares its own real dependency and receives B's include directory.
Mistake to avoid: changing A to PUBLIC B just to leak the include path, which makes every consumer of A depend on B and exposes an implementation detail.
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.
